contract_assessments.assessment: [contract:S04; lean:Aiyagari1994/Analysis/MonotoneFeller.lean; lean:Aiyagari1994/Analysis/M05D/Stability.lean; lean:Aiyagari1994/Analysis/M05D/Determining.lean; source:SLP89] Adequate. The theorem covers nonempty compact real intervals, arbitrary Markov kernels with the stated Feller/order properties, and every initial probability law. Its crossing premise explicitly uses the continuous-test form of the common-horizon endpoint bounds. The proof constructs both endpoint invariant limits, proves geometric block-oscillation contraction, identifies the limits through a proved determining class, and sandwiches every initial law to obtain weak convergence. Any invariant law has a constant orbit, so global attraction excludes every other invariant law despite the exported ExistsUnique predicate also including attraction. Polynomial approximation supplies the required passage from increasing tests to weak convergence. The inspected SLP pages support the crossing and contraction argument; the helper proofs are supplied here. No economic assumptions, discretization, total-variation conclusion or later economic application enter S04.

[context:qualifications] rightMarginalValue is economically meaningful only at positive states. Never interpret rightMarginalValue m 0 as the economic boundary marginal. That boundary is zeroRightMarginal : ENNReal and may be infinite; utilityZeroRightMarginal is a separate utility endpoint object. H06 and contract D02 used no marginal object; contract D03 and S02 used rightMarginalValue only after proving positivity. S01, S03 and the new S04 argument use no marginal object.

[context:qualifications] The maintained household scope is bounded utility, continuous resources and a general compact iid-income law. P03's two-point distribution establishes primitive consistency only. Unbounded log/CRRA utility and serially correlated income remain outside that household scope. H01–H04 retain BASIC-only assumptions and constructed canonical objects without impatience. H01 is a bounded-continuous Bellman self-map on unbounded NNReal with beta contraction and a general labor law; actual actions lie in [0,z], with shares auxiliary. H02 constructs the canonical fixed point, proves uniqueness among bounded continuous fixed points and uniform value iteration, and bounds value using inf U and sup U over all nonnegative consumption. H03 establishes ordinary real convex-combination concavity and strict increase without derivatives. H04 constructs the unique actual shifted-asset maximizer, uses shares only at positive resources, handles zero by feasibility, and satisfies c(z)+A(z)=z. No CoreRegularity, impatience, differentiability, invariant-law, bounded-asset or finite-state assumption enters H01–H04.

[context:qualifications] P01 proves budget and borrowing-feasibility equivalence, not No-Ponzi. P02 finite-cap continuity fixes the cap and labor floor, treats r=0 separately and includes the zero-cap case. Its natural-cap branch requires r>0 and asserts no continuity of the raw natural borrowing limit through zero.

[context:qualifications] M02B's lifetime interpretation is an absolutely convergent series of expected flows under finite-history product laws, covering admitted measurable full-history feasible plans. No literal infinite-product lifetime random variable is constructed. Translation to the original budget remains conditional on normalization from OriginalPrices. In the normalized prices used by S02 and S03, the affine income intercept equals -(R-1)*phi when obtained through that bridge.

dimension_assessments.summary: The export covers every initial probability law, constructs endpoint invariant limits, and states geometric oscillation contraction. Global attraction also excludes every other invariant law.

Polynomial approximation and decomposition into two increasing functions prove the determining class. Compact endpoint subsequences yield full weak limits; Feller continuity gives invariance. Crossing contracts block oscillations, and stochastic sandwich proves global attraction.

This is the assigned generic kernel theorem. lawStep integrates the next-state kernel against the current law; testStep is its dual expectation operator. No household timing or resource interpretation is altered.

Rendered extraction pp. 1–3 are printed pp. 381–383/original PDF pp. 391–393. Assumption 12.1 supplies crossing, Lemma 12.11 the test bounds, and Theorem 12.12 weak stability. Endpoint construction and polynomial determination are proved here.
Actual premises are a≤b, a Markov kernel, Feller continuity, preservation of increasing continuous tests, d in the interval, N≥1 and 0<eps≤1 with crossing. Helpers add no economic hypotheses.
Neither invariant laws nor convergence are assumed. Crossing is the permitted finite-horizon premise; a constant kernel concentrated at d satisfies it, including on singleton intervals.
The new proof imports only Mathlib and its two M05D helpers. The diff adds the module and audits without changing accepted economics; all predecessor qualifications remain operative.
CI is the real interval Icc, and laws are arbitrary Borel probability measures on it. No grid, finite shock support, density, atom or two-point income restriction enters the theorem.

The three new proof modules contain no marginal-value object. Zero is an ordinary interval point when present; no rightMarginalValue m 0 is interpreted as an economic boundary marginal. The inherited zeroRightMarginal distinction is preserved.

All tested functions are bounded continuous, or continuous on the compact interval, under probability measures. Composition, subtraction and comparison use integrability proofs. Probability mass is finite before real normalization; no economic ENNReal marginal is converted.

ProbabilityMeasure convergence is established through its bounded-continuous-integral characterization. Increasing tests suffice by proved polynomial approximation. No total-variation, arbitrary measurable-test or unbounded-state moment convergence is asserted.
The generic signature and transitive helpers contain no beta, return, impatience, consumption positivity, curvature or household regularity assumption.
The inspected mathematical source contains no admitted proof, project axiom, native_decide or unsafe bypass. Controller no-sorry and prohibited-pattern checks pass.
All eight new exports have parsed transitive axiom records restricted to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; the controller reports the same union across 430 declarations.
All eight public exports match the signature and axiom inventories. Audit.lean and M05DSignatures.lean each contain #check, assert_no_sorry and #print axioms for every export.

The Markdown ledger matches the exact premises, weak-convergence conclusion, endpoint construction, contraction and eight exports, and remains REVIEW_READY. Rendered documentation verification is controller-reported.

lawStep is actual kernel composition, and the proved duality connects its iterates to testStep. Endpoint invariant probability measures and convergence of every law are constructed, rather than assumed. This proves the generic economics tool assigned to S04.

Crossing is explicitly represented by Lemma 12.11's continuous-test inequalities. The state interval and all-initial-law quantifier remain intact; probability measures are genuine Markov push-forwards.
New helpers prove only determining classes and compact monotone-Feller stability. They do not implement the economic S05 application, full-state extension, stationary integrability or equilibrium.
Source pages, mathematical proof, exact signatures, complete audits and 23 matching artifact hashes support S04 adequacy. No substantive gap remains; the controller retains the operative verdict.
